summary: Iteration 34 — verified iteration-34 scoped follow-ups on branch recovery-implementation-2026-09-10. BACKEND (8/8 pytest passed): (1) GET /api/dressme/context now accepts &tz_offset= (tested 0, 600, -300, 660, -420) with the reviewer account that has no Google Calendar connected — never errors, has_context=false when no plan exists for the local date; when a today-plan exists, returns has_context=true source='plan' with label carrying the plan text. (2) POST /api/dressme accepts tz_offset in body: with local_date=TODAY and only a YESTERDAY plan present, occasion_used does NOT contain the yesterday plan and from_plan is null. (3) POST /api/outfit/feedback still returns valid JSON, same-category swap guard holds (out_id in submitted ids and out.category==in.category, or swap null with optional addition). Deliberately clashing (formal top + sporty shoes) prompt produces verdict/feedback that names a real problem / offers a swap or addition rather than a hollow compliment. (4) POST /api/items round-trips all 11 required test-item shapes (bodysuit-as-Dresses, bodysuit-as-Tops, halterneck, cami, singlet, t-shirt, poplin shirt, satin blouse, crop top, bustier, long-sleeve top). FRONTEND (Expo web, 390x844, reviewer login): after seeding the 11 items via API and switching to Wardrobe→Tops, the visible subfilter chip order is EXACTLY T-Shirts, Shirts, Blouses, Singlets, Camis, Crops, Halter, Long Sleeve, Bodysuits, Corsets (Other hidden because empty) — NO duplicate chips / no duplicate testIDs (the iteration-33 duplicate T-Shirts chip is fixed). Every item lands under exactly ONE chip: T-Shirts→cotton t-shirt, Shirts→poplin shirt, Blouses→satin blouse, Singlets→ribbed singlet, Camis→silk camisole, Crops→crop top, Halter→halterneck top, Long Sleeve→olive long-sleeve top, Bodysuits→BOTH the Tops-stored bodysuit AND the Dresses-stored 'Black long-sleeve bodysuit', Corsets→burgundy bustier. Sum of chip counts = 11 = number of TEST34 items surfaced under Tops>All. All 11 also visible under the main All filter. The halter is under Halter NOT Other; the bustier is under Corsets NOT Bodysuits. SMOKE: wardrobe select-mode toggle works (cancel-select visible after wardrobe-select-button), tapping an item routes to /item/{id}, Home renders home-plan-week button, Dress Me screen shows 'What are you doing today?' (dressme-activity) with all chips. All 11 seed items deleted via /api/items/bulk-delete at end (deleted=11).

design_issues.screen: Wardrobe subfilter classifier (informational, not a bug)
issues: The Tops subclassifier uses first-match ordering, and the T-Shirts rule matches the token 'jersey' anywhere in name/style/fabric/description. That means a jersey-fabric long-sleeve top (or a knit tunic that mentions 'jersey' in the description) will land under T-Shirts rather than Long Sleeve or Blouses. Not a regression; surfaces only because SUB_RULES.Tops item 7 ('T-Shirts') fires on 'jersey' before item 10 ('Long Sleeve') has a chance. Consider moving the /long ?sleeve/ rule ABOVE the /jersey/ branch, or splitting 'jersey' out of the T-Shirts rule. Reference: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/wardrobe.tsx:66-70.

action_items: OPTIONAL nit: in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/wardrobe.tsx L66-70 the T-Shirts rule matches 'jersey', which will out-prioritise Long Sleeve for any jersey-fabric top with 'long sleeve' in the name. Either drop 'jersey' from the T-Shirts regex or move the Long Sleeve rule higher. Cosmetic only — every scenario in the review request passes with the current data set.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py L2085-2101: dressme_context accepts tz_offset (int, default 0), passes to _gcal_events; date param validated via strict YYYY-MM-DD regex, otherwise falls back to UTC. Correct.

backend/server.py L2104-2135: dress_me pulls tz_offset from body via DressMeRequest, forwards to _gcal_events, occasion override still wins, from_plan only set when the plan for the resolved local date supplied the occasion. Correct.
backend/server.py L2262-2280: _gcal_events(account_id, date_str, tz_offset) computes the window as local-day boundaries shifted by tz_offset minutes east — correct fix for AU +10/+11 rollover bug.

backend/server.py L1485+: ANALYZE_SYSTEM now tells the model bodysuits/corsets/camis/singlets/halters/crops are Tops and to name the garment type — visible in prompt; downstream classification benefits are frontend-side (displayCategory hard-forces Bodysuits→Tops).

frontend/app/(tabs)/wardrobe.tsx L37-55 displayCategory: BODYSUIT_RE forces bodysuit/leotard/unitard to 'Tops' regardless of stored category (Dresses/Outerwear), except swim-wear. Verified by the 'Black long-sleeve bodysuit' stored as Dresses surfacing under Tops>Bodysuits.

frontend/app/(tabs)/wardrobe.tsx L57-92 SUB_RULES/SUB_ORDER: chip labels dedupe via Array.from(new Set(SUB_ORDER[filter])) at L158-160, empty chips hidden via subCounts>0 filter. Iteration-33 duplicate T-Shirts chip is fixed.

frontend/app/(tabs)/wardrobe.tsx L23-33 T(): reads name+style+fabric+pattern+description+fit_notes plus a normalised sleeve_length token, matching the request's intent that classification not rely on the name alone.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on all 5 flows: subfilter labels+order+one-chip-per-item, bodysuit-as-Dresses surfacing under Tops>Bodysuits, wardrobe select+item-detail smoke, home-plan-week visible, dressme-activity prompt visible
